Pruning & Rooting Phylogenetic Trees with ggTree

Shawn Xinyu Wang

April 15, 2025

Goals

  1. Load the FastTree2 unrooted tree that we calculated in analysis/04A_Phylogenetic_Tree_Construction.Rmd and `raw_preprocessed_physeq``.
  2. Merge the unrooted tree to the raw_preprocessed_phyloseq object.
  3. Visualize and inspect tree with ggtree.
  4. Evaluate long branches & prune ASVs, if needed. If your dataset has long branches, you will need to do this before rooting!!
  5. After pruning, root the tree, ideally within the Archaea and, if not, mid-root the tree.
  6. Combine the new, rooted tree with the phyloseq object.
  7. Save 2 phyloseq objects: 1. Unrooted tree phyloseq object, 2. Rooted tree phyloseq object.

Inputs

  1. Our previously pre-processed phyloseq object that has chloroplasts, mitochondria, reverse complements, and negative controls removed, which is located in data/03_PreProcessing/raw_preprocessed_physeq.
  2. The raw, unrooted maximum liklihood tree that we generated using FastTree2, which is located in data/04_PhylogeneticTree/ASVs_unrooted.tree

Outputs

  1. The output of this file will be a S4 phloseq objected called phytree_preprocessed_physeq, which we will save to data/04_PhylogeneticTree/.

Timing of this script

Let’s record how long this file took to run on the class server, which we will record at the end of the script.

# What time did we start running this script? 
start_time <- Sys.time()

Set my seed

# Any number can be chosen 
set.seed(20020206)

Load Packages

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("phylobase")

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, phyloseq, ggtree, phytools, tidytree, phylobase,
               install = FALSE)

1. Load Data files

# Preprocessed phyloseq object 
load("data/03_PreProcessing/raw_preprocessed_physeq.RData")

# Inspect the phyloseq object 
raw_preprocessed_physeq
## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 1207 taxa and 173 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 173 samples by 52 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 1207 taxa by 7 taxonomic ranks ]
# Load in the tree! 
unrooted_tree <- read.tree("data/04_PhylogeneticTree/ASVs_unrooted.tree")

# Take a look at the tree
unrooted_tree
## 
## Phylogenetic tree with 1207 tips and 1205 internal nodes.
## 
## Tip labels:
##   ASV_0978, ASV_0823, ASV_0352, ASV_0840, ASV_0734, ASV_1064, ...
## Node labels:
##   , 0.000, 0.891, 0.648, 0.000, 0.970, ...
## 
## Unrooted; includes branch length(s).
str(unrooted_tree)
## List of 5
##  $ edge       : int [1:2411, 1:2] 1208 1209 1210 1211 1212 1213 1213 1214 1214 1215 ...
##  $ edge.length: num [1:2411] 0.00054 0.01565 0.00282 0.00053 0.01911 ...
##  $ Nnode      : int 1205
##  $ node.label : chr [1:1205] "" "0.000" "0.891" "0.648" ...
##  $ tip.label  : chr [1:1207] "ASV_0978" "ASV_0823" "ASV_0352" "ASV_0840" ...
##  - attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo"
##  - attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise"

2. Merge Unrooted Tree & raw_preprocessed_physeqn

Now that we’ve loaded in both our raw_preprocessed_physeq and the unrooted tree, let’s merge them into one phyloseq object that can be used to plot the tree with ggtree.

# Intuition check 
stopifnot(ntaxa(raw_preprocessed_physeq) == ntaxa(unrooted_tree))
# No news is good news! 

# Merge the tree with the phyloseq object 
unrooted_physeq <- 
  merge_phyloseq(raw_preprocessed_physeq, unrooted_tree)

# Let's take a look! 
unrooted_physeq
## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 1207 taxa and 173 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 173 samples by 52 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 1207 taxa by 7 taxonomic ranks ]
## phy_tree()    Phylogenetic Tree: [ 1207 tips and 1205 internal nodes ]

3. Visualize and inspect tree with ggtree.

Now, let’s take a look

Kingdom Level Tree

# Make a basic tree with the domains 
kingdom_tree <- 
  ggtree(unrooted_physeq) + 
  # color tips by kingdom
  geom_tippoint(mapping = aes(color = Kingdom)) + 
  # add a title
  labs(title = "Unrooted Tree") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("firebrick3", "cornflowerblue", "grey")) + 
  # Move the legend to the bottom of the tree 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Look at it 
kingdom_tree

# Check if tree is rooted
is.rooted(unrooted_tree) # should be TRUE
## [1] FALSE

INTERPRETATION #1:The unrooted tree looks clean. All ASVs are classified as Bacteria, and there are no obviously long or isolated branches. This suggests good data quality, likely due to effective chimera removal and ASV length filtering.

4. Long Branches?

4a. Evaluate Long Branches

Kingdom Tree with Node Labels

Let’s put labels on our tree so we have a bit more flexibility

# Add internal node labels to the tree for easy inspection
kingdom_node_tree <- 
  kingdom_tree + 
  geom_text(aes(label = node), hjust = -0.5, vjust = -0.3, size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Unrooted Tree with Node Labels") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Plot the labeled tree
kingdom_node_tree

Objectively judge the long branch

branch_lengths <- unrooted_tree$edge.length

ggplot(data.frame(length = branch_lengths), aes(x = length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Branch Length Distribution", x = "Branch Length", y = "Count")

INTERPRETATION #2:There were no unusually long branches in the unrooted tree. We evaluated the tree visually with ggtree (with node labels), and quantitatively via the branch length histogram. Both showed that the vast majority of branches had short to moderate lengths, with no extreme outliers.Therefore, we did not remove any ASVs.

5. Root the Tree

# Check if the unrooted tree is already rooted
is.rooted(phy_tree(unrooted_physeq))
## [1] FALSE
# Root the tree at the midpoint between the two most distant tips
midpoint_rooted_tree <- 
  phy_tree(unrooted_physeq) %>%
  phytools::midpoint.root()

# Confirm the tree is now rooted
is.rooted(midpoint_rooted_tree)
## [1] TRUE
# Merge the rooted tree back into the phyloseq object
midpoint_rooted_physeq <- 
  merge_phyloseq(raw_preprocessed_physeq, midpoint_rooted_tree)

6. Plot Midpoint Rooted Tree

# Quick inspection of tree 
midpoint_rooted_tree_plot <-
  ggtree(midpoint_rooted_physeq) + 
  geom_tippoint(mapping = aes(color = Kingdom)) + 
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = Kingdom)) + 
  labs(title = "Midpoint Rooted Tree") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("firebrick3", "cornflowerblue", "grey"))

# Look at the tree 
midpoint_rooted_tree_plot

# Add nodes 
midpoint_rooted_tree_node_plot <- 
  midpoint_rooted_tree_plot + 
  geom_text(aes(label = node), hjust = -0.5, vjust = -0.3, size = 1.5) 

# View it 
midpoint_rooted_tree_node_plot

INTERPRETATION #3 The midpoint rooted tree appears finalized, with no additional suspicious ASVs or long branches. The branch length distribution supports that the tree is clean.

7. Save phyloseq objects

# Now, save midpoint rooted phyloseq object
save(midpoint_rooted_physeq, 
     file = "data/04_PhylogeneticTree/midpoint_rooted_physeq.RData")
